conviction_note: abs_move 15 (option-implied 18.9% is indicative only with a 67% ATM spread; the name's own median reaction is 13.7%) times a near-balanced p_up of 52. The peer prints since CYH last spoke (HCA's Q3 uninsured payer-mix hit flat at ~$400m against Q2, HCA tracking the upper half of its cut guide, UHS acute volumes +4.9%) and an 11% short float lean slightly up. Against that: CYH must swing operating cash flow from -$209m in H1 to +$509-709m in H2 to hold its own guide, the last two prints fell 12-14% each, and the sector sold off on both peer prints this week. The findings sum to +1.3 and the scaled number is +0.6. Both are small and agree in sign; the gap is just the p_up weighting.
bar: Revenue: consensus $2.78B (Earnings Whispers, https://beta.earningswhispers.com/go/w/CYH) to $2.80B (Benzinga snippet, https://www.benzinga.com/quote/CYH/earnings-forecasts), roughly agreeing. The company's own July guide implies a higher H2 run-rate: FY revenue $11.4-11.6B less H1 $5.79B gives H2 $5.61-5.81B, about $2.80-2.90B a quarter. FY adj EBITDA $1.30-1.375B less H1 $638m gives H2 $662-737m, about $331-369m a quarter; Q2 was $330m. Guide sources: Q2 8-K exhibit https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001108109/000119312526312454/cyh-ex99_1.htm and Quartr summary https://quartr.com/events/community-health-systems-inc-cyh-q2-2026_ofmIkPRB. EPS is DISPUTED: -$0.22 (Earnings Whispers), -$0.29 (Finviz, https://finviz.com/quote.ashx?t=CYH), -$0.30 (Benzinga), -$0.04 (Benzinga JP). Every EPS-dependent size is therefore capped small; the name trades on adjusted EBITDA and the guide.
positioning_check: Finviz (https://finviz.com/quote.ashx?t=CYH, read 2026-10-28): short float 11.19%, short interest 12.30M shares, short ratio 10.16 days to cover, float 109.88M, mean target $3.09 against $2.795 spot, recommendation 3.20 (hold to underweight). The baseline has no 25-delta skew (null). Put/call open-interest ratio is 0.67, but total open interest is only 267, so the options carry no usable directional statement. Tape: -2.3% over 20 days, -33.6% from the 52-week high, +12.3% off the low. CYH fell 3.4% on 2026-10-27 on 1.95M shares (about 1.8x its 20-day average) as HCA and UHS reported. A 10-day days-to-cover is a crowded short, which shrinks the negatives.

findings.finding: HCA's Q3 release (2026-10-27) puts its uninsured-driven payer-mix headwind at about $400m pre-tax, the same figure HCA disclosed for Q2 on 2026-07-14. So the exchange-loss-to-uninsured shift did not accelerate in Q3. HCA also says FY results will land in the upper half of the ranges it cut in July, and its Medicaid supplemental-payment net benefit 'modestly increased'. CYH cut its own guide on 2026-07-22 on the same uninsured shift and assumed H2 roughly equal to Q2; a peer showing the shift flat quarter on quarter is evidence that CYH's guide holds rather than takes a second cut. The market's bar is H2 at the low end of the guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: CYH fell 13.7% on its 2026-07-22 print, when it cut the guide on uninsured volumes, and 12.6% on 2026-04-21. It rose 25.8% on 2025-10-23 and fell 25.3% on 2025-07-23 (baseline). Guidance has been the line that moves it. HCA itself fell about 3.3% on 2026-10-27 despite the upper-half statement (Yahoo chart, https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/HCA?range=10d&interval=1d), so a sector reading 'in line' has not been paid this week.
findings.why_not_priced: It is a peer document from one day before CYH reports, and CYH sold off 3.4% in sympathy that day rather than rallying. If the market had read the quarter-on-quarter stability as good for CYH's guide, CYH would not have fallen with HCA. It sits 33.6% below its high with a 10-day short.
findings.independence: Q2 comparison point: HCA's $400m Q2 payer-mix loss in Healthcare Dive, https://www.healthcaredive.com/news/hca-cuts-2026-earnings-ACA-coverage-losses/825147/ (2026-07-14). That is a different document about the same company, so this is one peer, two readings.

findings.finding: UHS's Q3 release (2026-10-27) shows same-facility acute adjusted admissions up 4.9% (from +2.9% in Q2), but net revenue per adjusted admission down 1.7%, and supplemental Medicaid payments added $47m. Industry acute volume accelerated in Q3 while price and mix weakened. That fits CYH's Q2 pattern (same-store adjusted admissions +2.9%, unfavourable payor mix) and suggests CYH volumes held. The pricing decline offsets most of it.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Same-store volume beats have not driven CYH's reactions on their own; the 2026 prints moved on payer mix and guidance (baseline -13.7%, -12.6%). UHS's own stock fell about 4.5% on 10-27 and about 2.5% more on 10-28 (Yahoo chart, https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/UHS?range=10d&interval=1d).
findings.why_not_priced: It is a peer proxy, not a CYH number, and CYH's footprint (non-expansion Southern states, small markets) differs from UHS's acute book. The market's response to it was to sell the group, not to read through to volumes.
findings.independence: HCA same-facility equivalent admissions +3.0% and ER visits +5.1% in Q3 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000860730/000119312526432665/hca-ex99_1.htm) point the same way on volume. That is a different company and document.

findings.finding: CYH fell 3.4% on 2026-10-27 to $2.84 on 1.95M shares, about 1.8x its 20-day average, the day HCA and UHS reported, with no CYH-specific filing or release (EDGAR shows no 8-K since 2026-07-22). Some of the group's negative read-through is already in CYH's entry price.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior instance measured; the baseline's 5-day run-up is -0.9% and the 20-day is -2.3%.
findings.why_not_priced: This is a statement about what is priced: the sympathy sell-off lowers the bar into the print. If the peers had been read as positive for CYH, the stock would not be sitting at $2.79-2.81 into the release.
findings.independence: EDGAR submissions for CIK 1108109 show no 8-K between 2026-07-22 and 2026-10-28 (https://data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK0001108109.json), so the move was not company news.

findings.finding: Short interest is 12.30M shares, 11.19% of a 109.88M float, at 10.16 days to cover (Finviz, read 2026-10-28), on a $2.80 stock with a 7x-levered equity stub (about $9.55B long-term debt at 2026-06-30). A guide that holds can force covering into a thin float.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The +25.8% (2025-10-23) and +18.5% (2025-04-23) reactions show the upside tail when a print relieves the guide. The baseline carries no short-interest history.
findings.why_not_priced: Positioning is the price. What matters is that 10 days to cover on about 1.1M shares a day means a relief print cannot be covered in one session, and the option market is too thin (267 total open interest) to absorb it. If the short were already being covered, the 20-day tape would be rising, not -2.3%.
findings.independence: Debt level from CYH's Q2 10-Q, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1108109/000119312526314196/cyh-20260630.htm (2026-07-23), which also explains why the equity moves 12-26% on prints.

findings.finding: CYH's Q2 10-Q shows H1 2026 operating cash flow of -$209m (against +$208m a year earlier) and cash down to $149m at 2026-06-30. The FY guide of $300-500m operating cash flow therefore needs +$509-709m in H2, a swing that depends heavily on the timing of supplemental-payment receipts. Q3 cash flow, or a cut to the cash-flow guide, is a visible risk on a 7x-levered name even if EBITDA holds.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The 2026 prints that cut or pressured the outlook fell 12.6% and 13.7% (baseline). No separate cash-flow-only surprise is isolated in the record.
findings.why_not_priced: Previews and the consensus carry EPS and revenue, not the H2 cash walk. The OCF guide ($300-500m) appears only in the guidance table (https://quartr.com/events/community-health-systems-inc-cyh-q2-2026_ofmIkPRB), and the H1 deficit has to be read off the 10-Q. If the market were pricing a cash-flow cut, the 2031/2032 secured notes and the equity would have moved on it. Uncertain: CYH may simply show the expected seasonal receipt of supplemental payments. Sized net of the crowded short.
findings.independence: The Q2 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001108109/000119312526312454/cyh-ex99_1.htm) confirms the H1 operating cash use of $(209)m and the $600m tender funded from divestitures. It is the same company's numbers in a second document.

findings.finding: The Q2 10-Q shows CYH's self-pay net revenue more than doubling to $39m (from $18m) and charity care at standard charges up to $519m from $334m year on year. So the uninsured shift at CYH is larger in relative terms than its payer-mix share implies (self-pay went from 0.6% to 1.4% of revenue). An Earnings Whispers headline of 2026-10-20 (on Finviz) frames Q3 as an 'early test' of the freshly cut EBITDA guide on this uninsured surge.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2 print, where this surfaced, fell 13.7% (baseline, 2026-07-22).
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: it has been public since July and the guide was cut on it. What may not be priced is whether the CYH-specific uninsured rate kept rising in Q3 while HCA's flattened. Nothing CYH-specific since July answers that.
findings.independence: Earnings Whispers preview headline 'Community Health's Uninsured Surge Puts Freshly Cut EBITDA Guidance To An Early Test', listed on https://finviz.com/quote.ashx?t=CYH dated Oct-20-26 (headline only, body not read). It cuts against the first finding's HCA read.

findings.finding: Director William Norris Jennings sold 40,000 CYH shares on 2026-08-25 at a weighted $2.96, leaving 38,468 held directly. He sold just over half his position, about two months before the Q3 print.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No measured history for insider sales on this name.
findings.why_not_priced: It was a small ($118k) sale by a single non-executive director, two months ago and before quarter end, so it is weak evidence. Filed for breadth.
findings.independence: A Form 144 was filed the same day (EDGAR, https://data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK0001108109.json). It is the same transaction.

findings.finding: Consensus Q3 revenue of $2.78-2.80B sits at or below the low end of the H2 run-rate the company's own July guide implies ($5.61-5.81B for H2, or $2.80-2.90B a quarter, after H1 revenue of $5.79B). A revenue miss against the street is therefore less likely than a miss against the guide. This holds on a 60-hospital base with Q2 same-store revenue +2.4%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Revenue beats have not been CYH's driver; Q2 (EPS miss by $0.09 per MarketBeat, guide cut) fell 13.7%. Capped small because the EPS bar is disputed across four sources.
findings.why_not_priced: The arithmetic is simple and the street has likely set Q3 low for seasonality. The finding is small because a guide-consistent revenue number is what the company told the market to expect.
findings.independence: Consensus sources: https://beta.earningswhispers.com/go/w/CYH ($2.78B) and the Benzinga snippet ($2.80B). Guide ranges also in https://quartr.com/events/community-health-systems-inc-cyh-q2-2026_ofmIkPRB.

baseline_tension: There is no skew, and the option market is too thin to make a directional statement. The slight up-lean from peer stability and the crowded short runs against the name's recent habit of falling 12-14% on prints and against the sector's selling of both peer prints this week, so p_up stays near 50 (52).
lessons_applied: Rule 6 (lands inside the guide): the HCA uninsured-stability finding confirms what CYH already guided to (H2 ≈ Q2), so it went from +1.5 to +1.0.
Rule 1 (fact vs reaction): peers HCA and UHS both fell on in-line or upper-half prints this week, so the UHS volume finding went from +0.5 to +0.3 and p_up stayed at 52.
Rule 7 (crowded short at 10 days to cover): the cash-flow negative went from -1.5 to -1.2 and the director-sale finding from -0.3 to -0.2.
Rule 5 (an unexplained drawdown is worth 0): the sympathy sell-off has an explanation (the peer prints), so it was kept but cut from +0.5 to +0.3.
Self-pay/charity care finding went from -0.5 to -0.3, because it has been public since July and the guide was cut on it.
Rule 6 (disputed bar): the EPS bar runs -0.04 to -0.30 across four sources, so the revenue-bar finding was capped at +0.4 (from +0.5).
abs_move_pct (15) and p_up (52) are unchanged; rule 8 argued against shrinking abs_move below the name's 13.7 median.
